{{Short description|Theorem in mathematical finite group theory}}
In [[mathematics]], namely [[Group theory#Finite group theory|finite group theory]], the '''Baer–Suzuki theorem''', [[mathematical proof|proved]] by {{harvtxt|Baer|1957}} and {{harvtxt|Suzuki|1965}}, states that if any two elements of a [[conjugacy class]] ''C'' of a finite [[group (mathematics)|group]] generate a [[nilpotent group|nilpotent]] [[subgroup]], then all elements of the conjugacy class ''C'' are contained in a nilpotent subgroup. {{harvtxt|Alperin|Lyons|1971}} gave a short elementary proof.
